transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess I'm here because of some things happening at my job. I'm a waitress, and... what really scared everyone at work is that I started freezing up right in the middle of service. Or I'd start doing things completely out of order. 

Like, I'd end up just standing over by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, and I'd be repeating table numbers out loud instead of actually closing out the checks. It really freaked my coworkers out, so... that's why I'm here.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or found yourself talking more rapidly than usual, even if others told you you were acting out of the ordinary?

No, I don't think so. I haven't really had anything like that happen. I definitely haven't felt super energized or felt like I didn't need to sleep. And... no, no one has said anything about me talking too fast or anything like that. It's really just been the freezing up and getting confused during my shifts that people noticed.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with friends and family?

Yeah, I have. I used to do a lot of different things, but I don't really go for beach walks, bake, garden, or write in my journal much anymore. 

And it's affecting things at home, too. Like, when my husband tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there. It's not that I'm trying to ignore him or anything, it just feels like... I don't know, like I just can't get myself to care or even start anything at all.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the loss of interest and difficulty engaging in activities?

I guess this whole change in me has been building for a while now... probably about a year and two months. It seemed to start right around the time I was asked to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities at work.
Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

No, I wouldn't say I feel depressed or sad. It's not like a heavy, hopeless feeling... it's just more like I'm empty or blank. I just don't have the energy or desire to do anything, but I don't feel down in the dumps about it.
Have you noticed that your movements have slowed down, or that you feel restless and unable to sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel restless or jittery, and... well, I don't think I'm moving any slower than normal. I mean, I sit around a lot more now just because I don't have the drive to get up and do things, but my actual physical movements seem regular to me.
Have you noticed that things you used to find enjoyable, like baking or writing in your journal, no longer give you any satisfaction or pleasure?

Yeah, that's pretty much it. I don't really bake or write in my journal much anymore. I've stopped gardening and going for beach walks, too. I just don't get anything out of them now. It even affects things at home... like, when my husband tries to talk with me, I mostly just sit there. It just feels like I can't get myself to care or start anything.
Have you been experiencing a lot of fatigue or loss of energy, even when you haven't been doing much physically?

No, not really. I mean, I'm not physically tired or exhausted. It's more just... like I was saying, not having the motivation to start things. But my actual energy feels fine, I think. I just don't really use it.
Have you noticed that you’re doing much less than you used to, even in basic daily tasks like getting dressed, cooking, or cleaning around the house?

No, not exactly. I mean, I still get dressed and shower, and I can make a sandwich or something if I'm hungry. I'm not... I haven't stopped doing the basics. It's more just the hobbies and talking to people that I don't do. But I still manage to keep myself and the house somewhat put together.
Have you noticed that your lack of motivation or difficulty starting activities has been happening almost every day for at least two weeks at a time?

I haven't really kept track of it like that. I mean... I don't think it's been every single day for two weeks straight. It just feels like it happens a lot, but I couldn't say for sure if it's been that continuous without a break.
Can you tell me if the lack of motivation or difficulty starting activities has occurred on most days, for most of the time, over the past year or so?

I don't think so. I mean, it hasn't been going on for a whole year. It's more recent than that. I haven't been feeling this way for that long, just... lately, I guess. But definitely not most days for a year.
Can you tell me if there was a period of at least two weeks where you felt this way most of the time, nearly every day?

Like I was saying before, I really don't think it's been a solid two weeks. I... I just don't remember a time where it was that bad nearly every day for that long. There's usually a day or two in there where I feel a little more normal and can actually get up and do things. So, no, I don't think there was a two-week period exactly like what you're asking.
Can you think back and tell me if there was ever a time when you felt this way—like you couldn’t get yourself to do things—for at least two weeks straight, without much of a break?

I... I think you just asked me that. But no, like I said, I really can't think of any time where it lasted two whole weeks without a break. I always end up having a day in there where I can get up and, you know, go to my shifts at the restaurant or just do things around the house. So no, never two weeks straight.
Looking back, can you identify a specific time when you felt this way—like you couldn’t get yourself to do things—for at least two weeks in a row, without much of a break?

Doctor, I feel like we're going in circles here. You've asked me this a few times now. Like I said, no. I really haven't had a time where I couldn't do things for two solid weeks in a row. I always have a day or two where I get back on my feet and go to work or take care of things. It just hasn't been two weeks straight like you're describing.
Can you tell me if there has ever been a time when you felt low, empty, or sad most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

Doctor, I... I'm really starting to feel like you're not listening to me. You just keep asking the same thing over and over. Like I've been saying, no. I haven't had a time where I felt that way for two whole weeks straight. There's always a break in there where I feel okay enough to go to my shifts or just function normally. So, no, not for two solid weeks.
Over the past two years, have you had periods where you felt this lack of motivation or emptiness more days than not, even if not every single day?

No, not really. I mean, I have days where I just don't want to do anything, sure, but it's not like it happens more often than not. Over the last couple of years... no, I wouldn't say it's been most days. Just a day here and there, like anyone else, I guess. Nothing that stretches out like that.
Have you ever felt detached from yourself, like you were watching yourself from outside your body, or felt disconnected from the world around you?
No, I haven't. I mean, I've never felt like I was outside my body or watching myself like a movie or anything. I don't really get disconnected like that. I'm always just... right here in my own body.
Have you ever experienced times where things around you felt unreal, like the world seemed foggy or dreamlike, even if you weren't high or sleep-deprived?

No, nothing like that. The world always feels real to me. I don't get that foggy or dreamlike feeling you're talking about. Everything around me is just... normal, I guess. I haven't experienced anything like that.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks where you felt down, empty, or depressed most of the time, even if not every single day?
No, I haven't. I mean, I have bad days sometimes, but it's never been two weeks straight of feeling down or empty. It's just normal ups and downs, nothing that lasts that long.
Have you had times where you completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even if those times didn't last for two weeks straight?
No, not really. I still like doing the things I usually do. I haven't had a time where I just stopped caring about my hobbies or anything like that. I still enjoy my days off from the restaurant.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities without the full criteria for a major depressive episode, to differentiate between persistent depressive disorder (F34.1) and major depressive disorder (F32.9) or unspecified dissociative disorder (F44.89).
doctor.question: Have you had times where you completely lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even if those times didn't last for two weeks straight?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of interest or pleasure in activities) specifically in the context of depressive episodes (even if shorter than two weeks), building on the previous question about depression. While the patient's Negative Symptoms (S023) include a loss of interest in activities (beach walks, baking, gardening), the doctor's question is specifically screening for a depressive episode criterion (anhedonia) as a distinct mood symptom, not the negative symptoms of schizophrenia. Therefore, 'None' is the most appropriate response as the profile does not explicitly cover a distinct depressive episode.

patient.answer: No, not really. I still like doing the things I usually do. I haven't had a time where I just stopped caring about my hobbies or anything like that. I still enjoy my days off from the restaurant.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent difficulties in initiating and sustaining goal-directed activities, with a notable loss of interest and pleasure in previously enjoyed activities. These symptoms are consistent with an unspecified dissociative disorder, given the absence of depressive or manic episodes and the presence of dissociative-like symptoms such as emotional emptiness and functional disruption without a clear mood episode. The lack of duration criteria for major depressive episodes and absence of manic features excludes recurrent or single episode depression.
